flagged.evidence: The Definition says “A grid function is a real-valued function on all grid nodes” and then defines, “For grid functions v,w, ... the weighted interior inner product and norm” using only interior-node values. A nonzero grid function supported on the boundary has ⟨v,v⟩_h=0 despite v≠0, so this is not an inner product or norm on the stated space of all grid functions. It is positive definite on interior vectors (and on X_{h,0}), but the Definition does not restrict the domain there.
